One of the best Indie titles I've played in a long time. It's very short, more of a tech demo of what's to come.
Gameplay reminds me a lot of Shadow Warrior 2 with a hint of DOOM. Difficulty is a little above the average FPS making it a small but very entertaining challenge. The fact that it was just one guy who made this is mindblowing.

Outstanding combination of the legendary Titanfall and Outrider, people talk about stealing asset and whatnot. Can't expect much story with such a short game, mall glitches here and there, but what this team has achieve in term of graphic and shot&slash mechanics on a 10GB game is a really big middle finger to the so-called veteran developers out there. 

Kudos to the dev, I'll give all the star I can if steam ever have a star rating system.

At first i thought it was a souls-like game just like the tag says, but i think it’s closer to an isometric ARPG, which is fine, since i’m not a big fan of souls-likes anyway. What i really enjoyed is the exploration, the map isn’t huge, but it's full, and always feels rewarding. The combat and animations are smooth and satisfying (well, it’s moon studios, just look at Ori). The only problem for me is the performance issues in certain areas, but since it’s still in early access, i hope the devs will fix it up.

Sheepo is a charming metroid-platformer. It's very platforming heavy and varies in difficulty but hardcore platform fans would probably find it largely on the easy side. I struggled a bit here and there. There is no combat really, boss battles are pretty much platforming / dodging tests. 

It is short, but I appreciated what it had to offer, and it's speedrun friendly if you want to enjoy it more.

Good game. I bought it looking for a relatively mindless, easy shooter and this satisfied that itch pretty well. The story was decently engaging too, with lots of references and funny moments -  like a guy staring at an abstract painting going "do you think they hung it upside down?"

 There are a few different areas and a reused, small open-world area where you can "serve and protect" with side missions. It did crash several times with random "fatal errors", but the auto save is frequent enough to where it wasn't a major issue. It's fairly short, about 8-10hrs, so I'd say get it on sale.

Secret Agent Wizard Boy is deceptively simple; it is sandbox and immersive sim to the max. Any way you want to approach a challenge in this game, there's a spell for it, or there's a potion for it, or there's some item you can find or make somewhere for it. Absolutely nails the UE1 look as well, just an aesthetically successful and pleasing game. Don't think, just rush to buy the game now

Not particularly functional as of time of writing (repeated lobby issues, constant crash-to-menu bugs, and at least one whole lobby spawning out of bounds in less than an hour of play), but when it does work it's a rather goofy brand of magical mayhem. Getting into a firefight with someone where the two of you just hop around and shout "Fireball! Magic Missile! Freeze!" over and over is incredibly comedic. 

Plus, the game's $3. I might be more worried about the state it's in if it was asking for any more, but if I'm paying a solo dev less than a cheeseburger then I'm willing to put up with a bit more jank than average.

10 years of active development, 0 DLC, 0 microtransactions, a consistent $10 price tag with consistent 50% markdowns during any and all major steam sales.

Enough about the developers and marketing, lets talk about the game.

Amazing replayability, gameplay variety, length, and sense of consistent progression. The game has one of the best communities of any game I have ever played. Not to mention modding is now supported on steam (see Tmodloader) and the modding community is actually CRACKED.

I recommend everyone and their mother plays Terraria. Buy it.

Nice and simple puzzle adventure game with an interesting premise and artistic and stunning visuals. While very pretty to look at, it is not very engaging to play. Most of the puzzles are trivial, and the solution is immediately obvious, but the puzzle design is time-based, meaning you are required to do precise actions in a particular order during tight time windows. This, coupled together with very clunky controls, quickly becomes frustrating, and I would only really recommend this game to people looking for a mere cinematic experience.

The sub-par final act made me forget how good the rest of the game was,
Shrike ability gave so many I-frames it was hard not to use it to get through the last couple of bosses.

Half of the runs I get randomly disconnected, it is insane that this game has co-op but there is no way to have saves. It's not even that hard to implement it. I really expected more from this game, it's really fun, but when the game disconnects while we are having winning runs all that fun disappears. It's so disappointing that a game like this still has an issue that has such an easy fix and that this issue is still here after a lot of people complained about it. This game quickly became one of my favorite games ever. The aesthetics are immaculate, the boss designs and battles a real joy to go through, the soundtrack is wonderful, the story (as much as I could gather of it anyway) felt so familiar yet so foreign and unique at once. Part of me wishes I could delete all my memories of it and go through it from square one, because it's such a full experience to go through your first time. 
Even as someone who's not very good or experienced with metroidvania games, this really kept me going as I was so eager to see what the game would throw at me behind the next wall or boss. As well as, the exploring experience has been so fun and riveting to go through!

CloverPit is one of the most unique and addictive indie games I've played in a long time.

I actually played it on mobile first, and I enjoyed it so much that I ended up buying it on Steam as well. There's a surprising amount of content, and the Memory Packs add a lot of variety to each run. The game also has a great selection of interesting items, so experimenting with different strategies never gets old.

I also really like the visual style. The graphics have a unique charm that perfectly matches the atmosphere of the game.

My only real complaint is the lack of background music. The silence can make the game feel a bit empty at times, and I think a soundtrack would have made the experience even better.

Overall, if you're looking for something fresh, fun, and highly replayable, I definitely recommend CloverPit.

An excellent survival horror game which isn't too dissimilar to Resident Evil in many ways. It has a pretty brutal inventory management system which really makes you take only what is absolutely necessary.

It has some superb graphical visual quality. The mechanics in the game for traversing are unique. The story is excellent. The suspense is great. The audio with earphones is incredibly atmospheric and adds to suspense and it has plenty of jump scares.

The game is well balanced and fair. New Game+ on hard mode is much easier than your first run on normal mode as you have most of the needed upgrades. 

If you liked the Dead Space remake and the recent Resident Evil remakes in 3rd person, you will love this game! It is a very similar experience with an excellent story.

I wish I could recommend this game but I can't it's just too expensive. Not the physical amount of money you spend the mental and emotional toll, and possibly the cost of the new controller. The price comes with the fact that once you beat it to completion hard techno is now your favorite music. You are now addicted to killing bosses as fast as possible as flawlessly as possible striving for perfection that is nearly unachievable. The guilt of taking the bad ending and killing that child to shave time off the speedrun and get a better score. Things like that are the real price you pay playing this game, but if you can pay that toll and enjoy super fast paced combat filled with graphene katanas, fully automatic laser pistols, and bullet hell dodging teleports you probably will love this game.

Nemesis is scripted as hell, he is not even threat like mr.x is! he always appears in same spots. 0 puzzles, boss fights are easy and boring except last Stage 3. They didn't bother to even add original soundtrack! Graphics are gorgeous, and it plays excellent. Sadly, i’m disappointed, RE2 remake is masterpiece, this is not even close.
